relevance_note: Four-patient case series, each with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant: "We describe four unrelated patients evaluated at a single tertiary center, each carrying a distinct TNFAIP3 mutation".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; every value comes from that reading. A Python script (scratch only) assembled the JSON and the 20-row checklists, then checked JSON validity, schema fields, label consistency and that every span occurs verbatim. Table 1 (patients as rows) is short and was quoted by hand, not transcribed by script. WHO IS INCLUDED: the four index patients (labelled 'Patient A'-'Patient D' as in the Discussion; Table 1 uses A-D, case headings Case 1-4); relatives described as affected or genetically tested (Case 1: paternal aunt, maternal aunt, sister with neurodevelopmental delay; Case 2: father, paternal grandfather, paternal great-grandmother, the brother with oral ulcers; Case 3: maternal aunt who died of lupus; Case 4: father and mother, both tested negative, and older brother with anxiety/epilepsy). Relatives described only as 'unaffected' and not tested (Case 1 brother, Case 2 mother and other brother, Case 3 two sisters) were not given rows. Patient B's father is labelled 'the father of patient B' (Discussion wording) to keep him distinct from Case 4's 'His father'. family_label_in_paper uses the case headings ('Case 1'-'Case 4'); the paper has no pedigree labels. PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED PATIENTS summarised in the Discussion were given their own rows with source_reference_in_review: the male p.Pro247Leu patient (15, 16); the female p.Arg271* patient with oral ulcers and uveitis (2, 12, 22); the p.Trp168* patient with HA20 and DLBCL (24); the male p.Q379* HA20 patient (26) and his mother and grandmother with Behcet's (26). The 'patients with primary breast marginal zone lymphomas (25)' carrying p.Q379* got no rows (no individual detail). POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: 'identified in a patient with both HA20 and DLBCL, as found in the father of patient B (24)' is ambiguous; ref 24 may describe Patient B's father himself or a different patient. They are kept as separate rows; cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the paper does not clearly state a re-report. The paper explicitly says Patient A is not the earlier p.Pro247Leu patient ('our patient is female'). VARIANTS: strings copied exactly, including the thin spaces in 'c.740C > T'. Variant class 'nonsense' for B, C and D rests on 'Three out of four patients had non-sense mutations' plus 'Missense mutation p.Pro247Leu in patient A' (elimination); class left 'not reported' for the father and literature patients except the explicit missense p.Pro247Leu. Patient B inheritance recorded as 'inherited paternal' from 'Her father has HA20 of the same genetic variant' and 'definite genetic predisposition with her father sharing the same mutation'; the mother was not stated to be tested. Father's zygosity left 'not reported' (not stated for him). Grandfather 'also had HA20' but no variant is stated for him, so no variant row. The pathogenicity statements for p.Trp168* and p.Q379* cite ClinVar RCV accessions (RCV005102078.1, RCV005052457.1) and the one for p.Arg271* cites Infevers/INSAID refs (17-21); these are recorded verbatim as the authors' statements (harness may want to flag them as ClinVar-derived). No functional assays reported. is_proband = true for A-D as the index patient of each case, although the paper does not use the word 'proband'. Patient D: age at HA20 diagnosis not stated explicitly (testing followed the ED presentation at 13), so left 'not reported'; age at onset taken from Table 1 ('9 years'). CHECKLIST JUDGEMENTS: Patient A uveitis/ocular item left 'not reported' because only uveitis and retinal vasculitis were negative (narrow-vs-broad rule); vasculitis likewise. Patient A 'poor weight gain' -> growth failure observed; vaginal ulcers -> genital ulcers observed. Patient B tissue transglutaminase antibodies -> autoantibodies observed; fever with pericarditis not counted as recurrent fever; GI item left not reported (calprotectin mildly elevated, duodenal lymphoid aggregates, biopsies without clear celiac disease or IBD). Patient C infant watery/bloody stools with calprotectin 199 not counted as GI inflammation (not called inflammation). Patient D CRP 60.9 mg/L counted as elevated inflammatory marker (no reference range printed); interstitial lung disease marked excluded from 'pulmonary computed tomography (CT) scans were normal'. Father of B: 'aphthous ulcers' -> oral ulcers, DLBCL -> lymphoproliferation, 'significant cutaneous findings' -> skin lesions. Literature p.Q379* patient: anal ulcerations -> GI ulcers, skin abscesses -> skin lesions. Relatives: neurodevelopmental delay and epilepsy -> CNS involvement; diverticulitis -> GI inflammation; great-grandmother 'joint issues' and 'rheumatic fever' not mapped to arthritis/arthralgia or recurrent fever. HLA B51 negativity in Patient C not recorded as a phenotype. CONTRADICTIONS/INCONSISTENCIES: Patient C's treatment section says 'Her abdominal pain has resolved, and her appetite has normalized' although neither was described earlier for C (possible carry-over from Case 1); recorded abdominal pain as observed with that span. The abstract's 'periodic fever with arthritis' does not match any single patient as described (A has fevers with arthralgia without arthritis; C has arthritis without fevers). Patient A's anti-Smith IgG 23.1 units was 'negative a year later' (temporal change, recorded in detail). No direct contradictions requiring paired observed/excluded rows were found.
